category: Results II: datasets, plot groups & plot types, derived values, export, reports, operators & built-in variables
description: Postprocessing nodes not covered in the first Results chunk: the transformation, cut and utility datasets (Cut Point/Line 2D, Revolution 2D, Surface, Edge, Parametric Curve/Surface, Particle, Ray, Mirror, Array, Join, Sector, Isosurface/Contour datasets, Grid, Mesh, Time Average/Integral, Filter, Partition); 1D/2D/Polar/Smith plot groups; plot types (Volume, Isosurface, Multislice, Arrow Surface/Volume/Line, Line, Point Graph, Global, Histogram, Particle/Ray Trajectories, Radiation Pattern, Table Graph, Mesh, Max/Min, Principal Stress, Annotation) and plot attributes (Height Expression, Filter, Selection, Color Expression, Material Appearance, Transparency); derived values (line integration, averages, maxima, global matrix, tables); export (plot, image, mesh, table, player) and reports/presentations/result templates; and the expression language: differentiation, coupling and evaluation operators (d, dtang, mean, at, with, withsol, nojac, subst, prev, timeint/timeavg, integrate, sum, linper/lindev/linsol, env/bndenv, reacf, test, if/nif, up/down/side, realdot, ppr/pprint, pmax/pmin/psum, timemax/timemin, isdefined/isnan/isinf, try_catch, smoothed step functions) and the reserved built-in variables (t, freq, lambda, phase, coordinates and normals, mesh variables, numberofdofs, constants) with the scoping rules for physics variables.

tools.name: Cut Point 2D / Cut Line 2D
tools.description: 2D versions of the cut datasets: Cut Point 2D evaluates the solution at given (x, y) coordinates (single points, grid or from a file) for point graphs versus time/parameter, and Cut Line 2D defines a straight line by two points (or a point and direction) with optional additional parallel lines to plot line graphs of a 2D solution along an arbitrary path. Cut Point 1D and Cut Line 3D / Cut Point 3D (already catalogued) are the other dimensions.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Cut Point 2D (cpt1) / Cut Line 2D (cln1); API: model.result().dataset().create("cpt1", "CutPoint2D"); cpt1.set("pointx", ...); model.result().dataset().create("cln1", "CutLine2D"); cln1.set("genpoints", new String[][]{{"0","0"},{"1","0"}})

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Source dataset (dset1).

parameters.name: pointx / pointy (Cut Point)
parameters.description: Coordinates; method: Coordinates | Grid | From file.

parameters.name: genpoints / method (Cut Line)
parameters.description: Two points or point and direction; 'Additional parallel lines' with distances.

parameters.name: snap
parameters.description: Snap points to the closest mesh vertex (Cut Point).

tools.notes: For a line along an existing edge use the Edge or the Line Graph plot directly on the solution dataset with an edge selection; cut datasets interpolate through elements.

tools.name: Revolution 2D
tools.description: Transformation dataset that sweeps a 2D axisymmetric (or plain 2D) solution around an axis to produce a 3D dataset, so results of axisymmetric models can be shown as full or partial 3D solids (start/revolution angle), with the option to revolve about a different axis and to include the deformation. COMSOL creates one automatically (rev1) for every 2D axisymmetric component.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Revolution 2D (rev1); API: model.result().dataset().create("rev1", "Revolve2D"); rev1.set("startangle", -90); rev1.set("revangle", 225)

parameters.name: startangle / revangle
parameters.description: Start angle and sweep angle in degrees (225 default gives a cut-away view).

parameters.name: Axis data
parameters.description: Revolution axis from the component (r = 0) or user defined.

parameters.name: Advanced: resolution
parameters.description: Number of angular divisions; spatial variables in the 3D dataset are named x, y, z (mapped from r, phi, z).

tools.notes: Revolution 1D turns a 1D axisymmetric solution into 2D. Azimuthal mode number solutions (2D axisymmetric with m > 0) are expanded with the correct phase when plotting.

tools.name: Surface / Edge 3D (datasets)
tools.description: Selection datasets restricting a 3D solution to chosen boundaries (Surface) or edges (Edge 3D), yielding a lower-dimensional dataset with its own coordinate system on which 2D-style plots (surface-parameter line graphs, contour on a face) and evaluations can be made, e.g. plotting a quantity on a curved face flattened, evaluating along an edge with arc length as x-axis, or using the boundary as a base for Height Expression plots. Edge 2D is the 2D analogue.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Surface (surf1) / Edge 3D (edg1); API: model.result().dataset().create("surf1", "Surface"); surf1.selection().set(new int[]{3}); model.result().dataset().create("edg1", "Edge3D"); edg1.selection().set(...)

parameters.name: selection
parameters.description: Boundaries or edges.

parameters.name: Parameterization (Surface)
parameters.description: Coordinates used for 2D plots on the surface: x, y, z or surface parameters.

tools.notes: Plots on a Surface dataset are 2D plots in the Surface's coordinates; to show them on the 3D geometry use the 3D plot group with a Selection attribute instead.

tools.name: Parametric Curve 3D / Parametric Surface (datasets)
tools.description: Datasets defined by coordinate expressions in one parameter (curve: x(s), y(s), z(s) over an interval) or two parameters (surface: x(s1,s2)...), used to evaluate and plot the solution along circles, helices, spirals, spheres or any analytic path/surface that is not part of the geometry - e.g. field on a sphere around an antenna, temperature along a spiral coil, pressure on a cylinder around a source. Resolution is controlled explicitly.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Parametric Curve 3D (pc1) / Parametric Surface (ps1); API: model.result().dataset().create("pc1", "ParCurve3D"); pc1.set("parmax1", "2*pi"); pc1.set("exprx", "R*cos(s)"); set("expry", "R*sin(s)"); set("exprz", "0"); model.result().dataset().create("ps1", "ParSurface")

parameters.name: parmin1 / parmax1 (parmin2 / parmax2)
parameters.description: Parameter ranges (s, or s1 and s2).

parameters.name: exprx / expry / exprz
parameters.description: Coordinate expressions.

parameters.name: res / res1, res2
parameters.description: Number of evaluation points.

tools.notes: Points outside the mesh evaluate to NaN; Parametric Curve 2D exists for 2D. For far-field patterns prefer the Radiation Pattern plot which handles the angular sweep itself.

tools.name: Particle / Ray (datasets)
tools.description: Datasets created automatically by the particle-tracing and ray interfaces holding the trajectories (positions and particle/ray variables versus time or path length) of all released particles or rays; they feed the Particle Trajectories / Ray Trajectories plots, the Particle/Ray 1D plots (variable versus time for every particle), Poincare maps, Phase Portraits, Spot Diagrams and the Particle Evaluation / Ray Evaluation derived values. Particle Bin and Ray Bin datasets group them by a variable for statistics, and Intersection Point datasets record crossings of a plane.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Particle 1 (part1) / Ray 1 (ray1) (automatic); API: model.result().dataset().create("part1", "Particle"); part1.set("solution", "sol1"); part1.set("physics", "cpt")

parameters.name: solution / physics
parameters.description: Solution and the particle/ray interface tag.

parameters.name: Particle/ray selection
parameters.description: Subset by index or logical expression (6.x).

parameters.name: Bin datasets
parameters.description: Particle Bin: bin by expression with number of bins and limits.

tools.notes: Requires the Particle Tracing or Ray Optics/Acoustics Module. Trajectories are stored at the study output times; increase the number of output times for smooth tubes.

tools.name: Mirror 3D / Mirror 2D (datasets)
tools.description: Transformation datasets that reflect a solution through a plane (3D) or line (2D) so a half or quarter model computed with symmetry conditions is displayed as the full geometry; vector components normal to the plane are flipped automatically for antisymmetric quantities when 'Vector transformation' is enabled. Chain two Mirror datasets for quarter models, and combine with Sector datasets for rotational symmetry.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Mirror 3D (mir1) / Mirror 2D; API: model.result().dataset().create("mir1", "Mirror3D"); mir1.set("data", "dset1"); mir1.set("planetype", "yz"|"xz"|"xy"|"general"); mir1.set("x", 0)

parameters.name: planetype / axis
parameters.description: Mirror plane (xy, xz, yz or general via point and normal) / mirror line in 2D.

parameters.name: Vector transformation
parameters.description: Flip normal components of vector fields on the mirrored side (6.x).

parameters.name: Include original / Remove interior boundaries
parameters.description: Keep the source half and merge faces on the symmetry plane.

tools.notes: Integrations over a mirrored dataset count both halves; derived values should normally use the original solution dataset.

tools.name: Array 3D / Array 2D (datasets)
tools.description: Transformation datasets that replicate a solution in a regular linear or rectangular array with given displacements and counts, for showing the full periodic structure (unit cell of a metamaterial, one pitch of a motor, one tooth of a heat sink) from a single-cell solution; optional Floquet phase shifts (6.x) apply the correct phase per copy for periodic wave problems.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Array 3D (arr1); API: model.result().dataset().create("arr1", "Array3D"); arr1.set("data", "dset1"); arr1.set("xsize", 5); arr1.set("ysize", 1); arr1.set("zsize", 1); arr1.set("xdisplacement", "a")

parameters.name: xsize / ysize / zsize
parameters.description: Number of copies per direction.

parameters.name: xdisplacement / ydisplacement / zdisplacement
parameters.description: Spacing per direction (expressions with parameters allowed).

parameters.name: Floquet periodicity
parameters.description: Apply exp(-i k.d) phase per copy.

tools.notes: The copies share the same solution; use the Sector dataset for rotational repetition with azimuthal mode phase.

tools.name: Join (dataset)
tools.description: Dataset combining two solutions (or two solution numbers/times/parameters of the same or different studies) so expressions can reference both: Difference (data1 - data2, e.g. compare two mesh sizes or designs, subtract a background), Sum, Product, Quotient, General (expression in data1() and data2()) or Explicit. It is the tool for convergence checks, error maps against a reference and before/after comparisons; the solutions must be defined on the same geometry (meshes may differ).
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Join (join1); API: model.result().dataset().create("join1", "Join"); join1.set("data", "dset1"); join1.set("solnum", 1); join1.set("data2", "dset2"); join1.set("solnum2", 1); join1.set("method", "difference"|"sum"|"product"|"quotient"|"general"|"explicit")

parameters.name: data / data2
parameters.description: The two datasets.

parameters.name: solnum / solnum2 (or time/parameter)
parameters.description: Which solution of each dataset.

parameters.name: method / expression
parameters.description: Combination method; General uses data1(expr) and data2(expr) inside the plot expression.

tools.notes: For time-dependent comparisons use the Time Average/Time Integral datasets or the with()/at() operators within one dataset.

tools.name: Sector 3D / Sector 2D (datasets)
tools.description: Transformation datasets that rotate a sector solution about an axis N times to reconstruct a rotationally periodic geometry (electric machines, impellers, bladed disks, antenna arrays), applying the azimuthal mode number phase (and vector rotation) for cyclic-symmetry eigenmodes and Floquet sectors. Combine with Mirror datasets when the sector itself has a symmetry plane.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Sector 3D (sec1); API: model.result().dataset().create("sec1", "Sector3D"); sec1.set("data", "dset1"); sec1.set("nsectors", 8); sec1.set("axistype", "z"); sec1.set("invtrans", "rot")

parameters.name: nsectors
parameters.description: Number of sectors in the full geometry.

parameters.name: axistype / axis point
parameters.description: Rotation axis.

parameters.name: Azimuthal mode number / Transformation
parameters.description: Phase per sector for cyclic symmetry modes; vector rotation on/off.

parameters.name: Start sector / sectors to include
parameters.description: Show a subset of the full circle.

tools.notes: Plots of a Sector dataset are visual reconstructions; integrate on the original sector and multiply by nsectors for totals.

tools.name: Isosurface / Contour (datasets)
tools.description: Datasets that extract the isosurfaces (3D) or contour lines (2D) of an expression at given levels as new geometric datasets, so other quantities can be plotted or integrated on them - e.g. the area of the T = 300 K surface, the heat flux through an isotherm, arrows on an isosurface, or a line graph along a contour. Unlike the Isosurface/Contour plots they produce evaluable geometry, not just graphics.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Isosurface (iso1) / Contour (con1); API: model.result().dataset().create("iso1", "Isosurface"); iso1.set("expr", "T"); iso1.set("levelmethod", "levels"); iso1.set("levels", "300 350")

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Level-set expression.

parameters.name: levelmethod / number / levels
parameters.description: Number of equally spaced levels or explicit list.

parameters.name: Resolution
parameters.description: Element refinement used when extracting the surface.

tools.notes: Isosurfaces are extracted per element with linear interpolation; refine the mesh or the resolution for smooth surfaces.

tools.name: Grid 1D / 2D / 3D (datasets)
tools.description: Datasets that define a regular grid of points (no solution required) on which functions, parameters and analytic expressions can be plotted and evaluated: visualise a global Function (interpolation, analytic, image) as a surface, plot an expression of x and y before any study, or resample a solution on a Cartesian grid for export (via the Interpolation of a solution in the grid's expressions with at()/with() is not needed - use Export > Data with 'Regular grid' instead). Grid datasets also serve Function plots and image functions.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Grid 2D (grid1); API: model.result().dataset().create("grid1", "Grid2D"); grid1.set("source", "data"|"function"); grid1.set("function", "int1"); grid1.set("par1", "x"); grid1.set("parmin1", 0); grid1.set("parmax1", 1); grid1.set("res1", 100)

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Function (global function to plot) or Data (empty grid for expressions).

parameters.name: par1/par2/par3, parmin/parmax, res
parameters.description: Parameter names, ranges and resolution.

tools.notes: Functions have a Plot button that creates these automatically. Grid datasets are also used by the Application Builder for visualisation without a solution.

tools.name: Mesh (dataset) / Time Average and Time Integral (datasets) / Filter (dataset)
tools.description: Utility datasets: Mesh makes a mesh (not a solution) available for plotting and evaluating mesh quality (qual, h, meshvol), element statistics and geometry-only expressions; Time Average / Time Integral compute the temporal mean or integral of a time-dependent solution over a time interval as a new (stationary) dataset for plots of mean fields (LES time averaging, cycle-averaged losses); Filter keeps only the part of a dataset where an expression satisfies bounds (e.g. theta_p > 0.5 in topology optimisation, or a region of high stress) and can export it as a mesh/STL; Partition splits a dataset by isolevels.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > Mesh (mesh1) / Time Average (tavg1) / Time Integral (tint1) / Filter (filt1); API: model.result().dataset().create("mesh1", "Mesh"); model.result().dataset().create("tavg1", "TimeAverage") (6.x type names: check Save as Java); model.result().dataset().create("filt1", "Filter"); filt1.set("expr", "dtopo1.theta_p"); filt1.set("lower", 0.5)

parameters.name: mesh (Mesh dataset)
parameters.description: Mesh tag to expose.

parameters.name: tstart / tend (Time Average/Integral)
parameters.description: Averaging interval; uses all stored time steps within it.

parameters.name: expr / lower / upper (Filter)
parameters.description: Filtering expression and bounds; 'Mesh import parameters' control the resulting mesh.

tools.notes: Mesh > Statistics (right-click a mesh) gives histograms of element quality without a dataset. Time Average on a large 3D transient is memory heavy because all stored steps are read.

tools.name: 1D Plot Group
tools.description: Container for graph plots (Line Graph, Point Graph, Global, Table Graph, Histogram, Function, Nyquist, Octave Band, Impulse Response, Waterfall...) with common x/y axis settings (log scale, limits, labels, secondary y-axis in 6.x), legend position, grid, title and the option to plot several solutions (all parameters/times or a selection) as separate curves. Every parametric/transient study creates one for probes automatically.
tools.usage: Results > (right-click) 1D Plot Group (pg1); API: model.result().create("pg1", "PlotGroup1D"); pg1.set("xlabel", "Time (s)"); pg1.set("ylog", true); pg1.set("legendpos", "upperleft")

parameters.name: data / looplevel
parameters.description: Default dataset and which solutions (parameters/times) to include.

parameters.name: xlabel / ylabel / xlog / ylog / axis limits
parameters.description: Axis settings (manual limits with xmin/xmax etc.).

parameters.name: legend / legendpos / titletype
parameters.description: Legend visibility and position, title mode.

parameters.name: Two y-axes
parameters.description: Secondary axis assignment per plot (6.x).

tools.notes: Export the curves with Export > Plot (data of a 1D plot) or copy the table from the plot. Polar and Smith plot groups are the special 1D containers for angular and reflection-coefficient data.

tools.name: 2D Plot Group
tools.description: Container for plots on 2D datasets (2D solutions, Cut Planes, Surface datasets, Revolution 1D, Grid 2D): Surface, Contour, Arrow Surface, Streamline, Line, Mesh, Annotation, Table Surface, Particle Trajectories (2D), Histogram and more, with plot-group-level settings for the view, axis equal scaling, colour legend, title, frame (spatial/material) and the plot-in-plane of a Cut Plane. Height Expression attributes turn a 2D surface plot into a 3D height map.
tools.usage: Results > 2D Plot Group (pg2); API: model.result().create("pg2", "PlotGroup2D"); pg2.set("data", "cpl1"); pg2.create("surf1", "Surface")

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Dataset (2D solution or a Cut Plane / Surface / Grid dataset).

parameters.name: view / axis
parameters.description: View node used (with axis limits) and equal-axes option.

parameters.name: frametype
parameters.description: spatial | material - frame for coordinates.

parameters.name: titletype / showlegends / edges
parameters.description: Title, colour legend and geometry edge display.

tools.notes: The '3D Plot Group' entry in the first Results chunk covers the 3D container; both share most settings.

tools.name: Polar Plot Group / Smith Plot Group
tools.description: Specialised 1D containers: the Polar Plot Group plots angle-dependent data (Radiation Pattern of far fields, Directivity, line graphs with an angle as x) on polar axes with dB or linear radial scaling; the Smith Plot Group (RF Module) plots reflection coefficients / impedances / admittances versus frequency on a Smith chart with Reflection Graph, Impedance Graph and Admittance Graph plots, reading S-parameters (emw.S11) or lumped-port impedances directly.
tools.usage: Results > Polar Plot Group (pg8) / Smith Plot Group (pg9); API: model.result().create("pg8", "PolarGroup"); pg8.create("rp1", "RadiationPattern"); model.result().create("pg9", "SmithGroup"); pg9.create("refl1", "ReflectionGraph")

parameters.name: Radial axis: linear/dB, limits
parameters.description: Polar group axis settings.

parameters.name: Reflection Graph: expr
parameters.description: Complex reflection coefficient, e.g. emw.S11; reference impedance for impedance/admittance graphs.

parameters.name: Angle range / zero angle position
parameters.description: Polar axis orientation.

tools.notes: Smith plots need the RF Module; polar plots are in the core product.

tools.name: Volume (plot)
tools.description: 3D plot rendering a scalar expression throughout the domains (colour on the outer boundaries of the selected domains, or with Filter/Selection attributes on a subset, and with Transparency to see inside), the 3D counterpart of Surface. It supports Deformation, Color Expression, Filter, Selection, Material Appearance and Transparency attributes and is the default plot for temperature, stress and potential in 3D.
tools.usage: 3D Plot Group > Volume (vol1); API: model.result("pg1").create("vol1", "Volume"); vol1.set("expr", "T"); vol1.set("unit", "degC"); vol1.set("colortable", "ThermalLight")

parameters.name: expr / unit / descr
parameters.description: Plotted expression, unit and legend description.

parameters.name: colortable / colortablerev / coloring
parameters.description: Color table (Rainbow, Jupiter, Thermal, Viridis...), reverse, or uniform colour.

parameters.name: rangecoloractive / rangecolormin / rangecolormax
parameters.description: Manual colour range.

parameters.name: resolution / smooth
parameters.description: Element refinement for plotting and smoothing between elements.

tools.notes: Volume plots only show what is visible from outside; use Slice, Multislice, Isosurface or a Filter attribute (e.g. x > 0) to look inside. The 'Surface', 'Slice', 'Contour', 'Streamline' and 'Deformation' entries in the first Results chunk cover those plots.

tools.name: Isosurface (plot) / Multislice (plot)
tools.description: Two ways to see scalar fields inside 3D domains: Isosurface draws surfaces of constant value (a number of levels or explicit levels, coloured by the level or by another Color Expression, optionally as a single surface per level), and Multislice draws colour maps on several parallel planes in the x, y and z directions (by number of planes or coordinates), which is the quickest overview of a 3D field. Both accept Deformation and Filter attributes.
tools.usage: 3D Plot Group > Isosurface (iso1) / Multislice (mslc1); API: model.result("pg1").create("iso1", "Isosurface"); iso1.set("expr", "T"); iso1.set("levelmethod", "levels"); iso1.set("levels", "300 320 340"); model.result("pg1").create("mslc1", "Multislice"); mslc1.set("xnumber", 3); mslc1.set("ynumber", 0); mslc1.set("znumber", 2)

parameters.name: levelmethod / number / levels (Isosurface)
parameters.description: Equally spaced count or explicit level list.

parameters.name: xnumber / ynumber / znumber or xcoord... (Multislice)
parameters.description: Number of planes per direction, or explicit coordinates (entry method).

parameters.name: colortable / interactive
parameters.description: Colour table; interactive slice position slider (6.x).

tools.notes: Isosurface Series and Contour Series (6.x) animate levels; the Isosurface dataset gives an evaluable surface instead of a picture.

tools.name: Arrow Surface / Arrow Volume / Arrow Line (plots)
tools.description: Vector plots drawing arrows for a vector expression on boundaries/2D domains (Arrow Surface), in 3D volumes on a regular grid (Arrow Volume, with x/y/z point counts or coordinates), or along edges/lines (Arrow Line), with arrow type (arrow, cone, 3D arrow), placement (grid, mesh nodes, Gauss points), normalisation (logarithmic, normalized, proportional) and scale factor. Combine with a Color Expression attribute to colour arrows by magnitude and with Streamline plots for flow fields.
tools.usage: Plot Group > Arrow Surface (arws1) / Arrow Volume (arwv1) / Arrow Line (arwl1); API: model.result("pg1").create("arwv1", "ArrowVolume"); arwv1.set("expr", new String[]{"u","v","w"}); arwv1.set("xnumber", 10); arwv1.set("arrowtype", "cone"); arwv1.set("scale", 0.5)

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Vector components (x, y, z expressions).

parameters.name: placement / xnumber / ynumber / znumber
parameters.description: Grid placement counts or mesh-based placement.

parameters.name: arrowtype / arrowlength / scale
parameters.description: Arrow style, length mode (proportional | normalized | logarithmic) and scale factor.

parameters.name: color / Color Expression attribute
parameters.description: Uniform colour or expression-based colouring.

tools.notes: Arrow Point (6.x) places arrows at point datasets; Coordinate System plots draw base vectors of coordinate systems.

tools.name: Line (plot)
tools.description: Plot drawing a scalar expression as colour (and optionally tube radius or line width) along edges in 3D or boundaries in 2D - beam/truss/pipe results (section forces, pipe flow velocity with the Pipe dataset), edge currents, boundary fluxes, or simply the geometry edges coloured by a quantity. Line type Tube with a radius expression shows magnitude as thickness (e.g. current in wires).
tools.usage: Plot Group > Line (line1); API: model.result("pg1").create("line1", "Line"); line1.set("expr", "beam.Mzl"); line1.set("linetype", "tube"); line1.set("radiusexpr", "abs(beam.Nxl)"); line1.set("tuberadiusscaleactive", true)

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Colour expression.

parameters.name: linetype
parameters.description: line | tube; tube radius expression and scale.

parameters.name: selection (via Selection attribute)
parameters.description: Edges to include.

tools.notes: Line Graph (1D) is the curve-versus-arc-length plot; the Line plot lives in 2D/3D plot groups.

tools.name: Point Graph / Global (plots)
tools.description: 1D graph plots versus time, frequency or a sweep parameter: Point Graph evaluates an expression at selected geometry points (or a Cut Point dataset) for each solution, and Global plots global scalar expressions (probes, integration operators, S-parameters, terminal currents, eigenfrequencies, parameters) with one curve per expression and per outer parameter. Both offer x-axis choice (time/parameter/expression), unit, legends, markers, line style and the Error Bars / Graph Marker attributes.
tools.usage: 1D Plot Group > Point Graph (ptgr1) / Global (glob1); API: model.result("pg1").create("ptgr1", "PointGraph"); ptgr1.selection().set(new int[]{3}); ptgr1.set("expr", "T"); model.result("pg1").create("glob1", "Global"); glob1.set("expr", new String[]{"emw.S11dB", "emw.S21dB"}); glob1.set("xdata", "expr"); glob1.set("xdataexpr", "freq")

parameters.name: expr / unit / descr
parameters.description: Expressions (Global accepts a list with units and descriptions per row).

parameters.name: xdata / xdataexpr / xdataunit
parameters.description: x-axis: time/parameter (default) or an expression.

parameters.name: linestyle / linecolor / linemarker / legend
parameters.description: Curve appearance and legend text (automatic or manual).

parameters.name: looplevelinput / looplevel
parameters.description: Which inner/outer solutions are plotted.

tools.notes: Global plots need a solution with several steps (time, parameter, frequency) to give a curve; for a single stationary solution use Global Evaluation instead.

tools.name: Histogram (plot)
tools.description: Plot showing the distribution of an expression over a domain/boundary/edge selection (weighted by element volume or count, as bars or a curve, in absolute or relative terms, with a chosen number of bins or bin limits) or of a particle/ray variable. Common for mesh quality, residence-time distributions, stress distributions in fatigue and particle energy spectra; Table Histogram and Matrix Histogram plot precomputed tables.
tools.usage: 1D/2D Plot Group > Histogram (hist1); API: model.result("pg1").create("hist1", "Histogram"); hist1.set("expr", "qual"); hist1.set("binmethod", "number"); hist1.set("number", 20); hist1.set("function", "discrete"|"continuous"); hist1.set("normalization", "none"|"peak"|"integral")

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Expression binned.

parameters.name: binmethod / number / limits
parameters.description: Number of bins or explicit limits.

parameters.name: function / normalization / cumulative
parameters.description: Bar (discrete) or line (continuous), normalization, and cumulative distribution option.

parameters.name: Weighting
parameters.description: Volume/area/length weighted or element count.

tools.notes: In 2D plot groups the Histogram becomes a 2D histogram (joint distribution of two expressions).

tools.name: Particle Trajectories / Ray Trajectories (plots)
tools.description: Plots rendering particle or ray paths from Particle/Ray datasets as lines, tubes, points, comet tails or ribbons, with the number of trajectories to show, the time or path length to plot up to, point/tube size expressions, and Color Expression attributes on any particle/ray variable (velocity, energy, intensity, wavelength); with a parametric time selection they animate directly through the Animation export. Ray Trajectories additionally handles ray splitting and can draw polarization ellipses.
tools.usage: 3D/2D Plot Group > Particle Trajectories (traj1) / Ray Trajectories (rtraj1); API: model.result("pg1").create("traj1", "ParticleTrajectories"); traj1.set("data", "part1"); traj1.set("linetype", "tube"); traj1.set("pointtype", "comet"); model.result("pg1").create("rtraj1", "RayTrajectories")

parameters.name: linetype / pointtype
parameters.description: line | tube | ribbon | none; point | comet | none.

parameters.name: Number of trajectories / particle selection
parameters.description: Limit or filter what is drawn.

parameters.name: tuberadiusexpr / pointradiusexpr
parameters.description: Size expressions (e.g. particle diameter).

parameters.name: Color attribute
parameters.description: Colour by expression such as cpt.V or gop.I.

tools.notes: Requires the corresponding module. Filter attributes work on particle variables (e.g. show only particles with status active).

tools.name: Radiation Pattern (Far Field) plot
tools.description: Plot (1D polar/2D/3D) of a far-field variable - emw.normEfar, emw.normdBEfar, gain/directivity, acoustics acpr.efc1.Lp_pfar, RCS - over a sphere or circle of angles around a chosen centre and radius, using the Far-Field Calculation / Exterior Field Calculation variables; in 3D it draws the pattern as a deformed sphere coloured by the value, in polar groups as a cut at a given azimuth/elevation. Options include dB scaling, normalisation to the maximum, the angular resolution and 'Include symmetry planes'. Formerly called Far Field plot.
tools.usage: 3D Plot Group > More Volume Plots > Radiation Pattern (rp1); Polar Plot Group > Radiation Pattern; API: model.result("pg5").create("rp1", "RadiationPattern"); rp1.set("expr", "emw.normdBEfar"); rp1.set("anglestepphi", 5); rp1.set("anglesteptheta", 5); rp1.set("radiusexpr", "1")

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Far-field expression (dB or linear).

parameters.name: anglestepphi / anglesteptheta (3D) / angle range (polar)
parameters.description: Angular resolution and range.

parameters.name: Normal / reference direction
parameters.description: Orientation of the pattern axes; cut plane definition for polar plots.

parameters.name: Scale / origin
parameters.description: Sphere radius scaling and centre.

tools.notes: Requires the RF, Wave Optics or Acoustics Module (far-field variables). Directivity/gain values are evaluated with Global Evaluation (emw.D, emw.gain) rather than from the plot.

tools.name: Table Graph
tools.description: 1D plot that draws the columns of a Results table (derived-value results, probe tables, imported measurement data from a Table node, optimisation histories) as curves, with a choice of the x-axis column and y columns, per-column styling and the option to transpose. It is the way to overlay experimental data on simulated curves and to plot values computed by Derived Values without re-evaluating.
tools.usage: 1D Plot Group > Table Graph (tblp1); API: model.result("pg1").create("tblp1", "TableGraph"); tblp1.set("table", "tbl1"); tblp1.set("xaxisdata", 1); tblp1.set("plotcolumns", "manual"); tblp1.set("plotcolumninput", new int[]{2, 3})

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: Table tag (Results > Tables).

parameters.name: xaxisdata / plotcolumns / plotcolumninput
parameters.description: x column index and which y columns to plot.

parameters.name: linestyle / linemarker / legend
parameters.description: Appearance and legends (from column headers).

tools.notes: Tables can be imported from text files (Results > Tables > Table > Import) or filled from MATLAB with model.result.table('tbl2').setTableData(). Table Surface, Table Contour, Table Point and Table Annotation plot 2D table data.

tools.name: Mesh (plot) / Max/Min (plot) / Principal Stress (plot) / Annotation (plot)
tools.description: Further plot types: Mesh draws the mesh elements (wireframe or coloured by quality/size, element filter by type) on solution or Mesh datasets; Max/Min Volume/Surface/Line/Point marks the maximum and minimum of an expression with their values and locations (and writes them to a table); Principal Stress Volume/Surface (structural) draws the three principal stress/strain directions as arrows scaled by magnitude; Annotation places text (with expressions evaluated, e.g. 'Tmax = eval(maxop1(T))') at coordinates or at the max/min position, and Table Annotation labels points from a table.
tools.usage: Plot Group > Mesh (mesh1) / More Plots > Max/Min Volume (mmv1) / Principal Stress Volume (pstrv1) / Annotation (ann1); API: pg.create("mesh1", "Mesh"); pg.create("mmv1", "MaxMin"); mmv1.set("expr", "T"); pg.create("pstrv1", "PrincipalStressVolume"); pg.create("ann1", "Annotation"); ann1.set("text", "Peak: eval(maxop1(T), degC) C")

parameters.name: Mesh: elementtype / expr / colortable
parameters.description: Elements shown and colouring (quality, size, none).

parameters.name: Max/Min: expr / display
parameters.description: Expression and how the markers/values are shown; results also go to a table.

parameters.name: Principal Stress: type
parameters.description: Stress or strain, arrow scaling, positive/negative colouring.

parameters.name: Annotation: text / position / latex
parameters.description: Text with eval() expressions, anchor coordinates, LaTeX markup support.

tools.notes: Max/Min plots evaluate on the plot's dataset and resolution, so their values can differ slightly from Derived Values > Maximum which uses element Gauss/Lagrange points.

tools.name: Height Expression / Filter / Selection (plot attributes)
tools.description: Attributes added under a plot to modify it: Height Expression lifts a 2D surface/contour plot into 3D by the plotted (or another) expression with a scale factor, giving 'carpet' plots of 2D fields; Filter shows only elements where a logical expression is true (x > 0, T > 350, dtopo1.theta_p > 0.5, particle variables) with element nodes to include control; Selection restricts the plot to chosen geometric entities (domains/boundaries/edges) without changing the dataset, and can inherit the selection from another plot.
tools.usage: Plot > (right-click) Height Expression (hght1) / Filter (filt1) / Selection (sel1); API: surf1.create("hght1", "Height"); hght1.set("scale", 0.5); surf1.create("filt1", "Filter"); filt1.set("expr", "z > 0"); surf1.create("sel1", "Selection"); sel1.selection().set(new int[]{2, 3})

parameters.name: Height: expr / heightdata / scale
parameters.description: Height from the plot expression or another one, scale factor, offset.

parameters.name: Filter: expr / nodestoinclude
parameters.description: Logical expression; include elements where all/any/... nodes satisfy it.

parameters.name: Selection: selection / inherit
parameters.description: Entities to plot; 'Apply to dataset edges' option.

tools.notes: Attributes belong to one plot; copy-paste them to apply to others. Deformation and Color Expression are covered separately.

tools.name: Color Expression / Material Appearance / Transparency (plot attributes)
tools.description: Appearance attributes: Color Expression colours an arrow, streamline, line, trajectory, isosurface or mesh plot by a second expression with its own colour table and range (e.g. arrows by speed, streamlines by temperature); Material Appearance renders surfaces/volumes with realistic material looks (from the material's Appearance settings: steel, aluminium, glass, copper, plastic families with custom colours, roughness and metallic settings, or by texture) for presentation-quality images with lighting/ambient occlusion in 6.x Visual Effects; Transparency sets per-plot alpha so interior plots and geometry are visible, with optional depth sorting.
tools.usage: Plot > Color Expression (col1) / Material Appearance (mtrl1) / Transparency (transp1); API: arws1.create("col1", "Color"); col1.set("expr", "spf.U"); col1.set("colortable", "Viridis"); surf1.create("mtrl1", "MaterialAppearance"); mtrl1.set("appearance", "custom"); surf1.create("transp1", "Transparency"); transp1.set("transparency", 0.6)

parameters.name: Color: expr / colortable / rangecolor*
parameters.description: Colour expression and scale.

parameters.name: Material Appearance: appearance / family / color / roughness
parameters.description: Material look; 'From material' uses the Appearance settings of the assigned material.

parameters.name: Transparency: transparency (0-1) / depthsort
parameters.description: Alpha level and ordering.

tools.notes: Material Appearance requires the surface plot's colouring to be 'Uniform' or the material settings are combined with the colour table; images with Visual Effects (ambient occlusion, shadows, 6.1+) need the OpenGL renderer.

tools.name: Line Integration / Surface Average / Volume Average / Surface & Volume Maximum/Minimum (derived values)
tools.description: Numerical evaluation nodes that integrate or average an expression over edges/boundaries/domains or find its maximum/minimum with the location, for one or all solutions (times, parameters) and write the result to a table - total current through a cross-section, mean outlet temperature, peak von Mises stress, drag force. Settings include integration order, the summation of components for vectors, and (for axisymmetry) whether to include the 2*pi*r factor. Point/Surface/Volume Integration and Global/Point Evaluation are in the first Results chunk.
tools.usage: Results > Derived Values > Line Integration (int1) / Surface Average (av1) / Volume Average (av2) / Surface Maximum (max1) / Volume Maximum / Volume Minimum; API: model.result().numerical().create("int1", "IntLine"); create("av1", "AvSurface"); create("av2", "AvVolume"); create("max1", "MaxSurface"); create("max2", "MaxVolume"); create("min1", "MinVolume"); then .selection().set(...); .set("expr", "..."); .setResult()

parameters.name: expr / unit / descr
parameters.description: Expression(s), output unit and description.

parameters.name: selection
parameters.description: Entities integrated/averaged/searched.

parameters.name: data / looplevel (solnum)
parameters.description: Dataset and which solutions to evaluate.

parameters.name: intorder / method (max/min)
parameters.description: Integration order; max/min evaluation on Lagrange or Gauss points.

parameters.name: table / setResult()
parameters.description: Target table; setResult() evaluates and writes.

tools.notes: Averages divide by the measure of the selection (length/area/volume), computed in the selected frame; results of vector expressions can be summed with 'Summation over components'. Evaluation Groups (already catalogued) collect several derived values into one table.

tools.name: Global Matrix Evaluation
tools.description: Derived value that evaluates matrix-valued global variables - S-parameter, capacitance, inductance, resistance, admittance/impedance matrices (emw.S, es.C, mfco.L, cir.Z...), stiffness/mass matrices exported from model reduction - into a table with one row/column per port/terminal, optionally as a Touchstone-style listing, in dB/phase or real/imaginary form. Used after Terminal/Port sweeps and Source Sweep studies.
tools.usage: Results > Derived Values > Global Matrix Evaluation (gmev1); API: model.result().numerical().create("gmev1", "EvalGlobalMatrix"); gmev1.set("expr", "emw.S"); gmev1.setResult()

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Matrix variable name (without indices).

parameters.name: Transformation
parameters.description: None | dB | Phase | Magnitude/Real/Imag for complex matrices.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: Table layout (matrix or list) and unit.

tools.notes: Requires the physics that defines matrix variables (AC/DC, RF, MEMS). Touchstone files (.s2p) are written by Results > Export > Touchstone (RF Module).

tools.name: Table (Results > Tables)
tools.description: Results tables hold the numeric output of derived values, probes, evaluation groups, Max/Min plots and optimisation, and can also be filled by import from text/CSV files or by the API (addRow, setTableData) to carry experimental data; each table has columns with headers/units, precision and display settings, and is the source for Table Graph plots, Table export and report inclusion. Accumulated probe tables collect probe values over sweeps.
tools.usage: Results > Tables > Table (tbl1); Table window toolbar (Copy, Export, Plot); API: model.result().table().create("tbl1", "Table"); tbl1.addRow(new double[]{...}); tbl1.getReal(); tbl1.getColumnHeaders(); tbl1.save("C:/out/t.txt"); model.result().table("tbl1").importData("file.csv")

parameters.name: addRow / setTableData
parameters.description: Append or replace rows programmatically.

parameters.name: getReal / getImag / getRowCount
parameters.description: Read table contents.

parameters.name: save(filename) / importData
parameters.description: Export to text/CSV/Excel or import from file.

parameters.name: Table properties: precision, format, units
parameters.description: Display and export formatting; 'Table settings' in the GUI.

tools.notes: The Table window shows the active table; 'Automatic table' behaviour creates a new one per derived value unless a table is chosen. In MATLAB use mphtable(model, 'tbl1').

tools.name: Plot (export) / Image (export)
tools.description: Export nodes writing plot data or pictures: Plot exports the numerical data behind a 1D plot (curves as columns) or the geometry/values of 2D/3D plots (points, elements, data) to text/CSV/VTK; Image renders a plot group to PNG/JPEG/BMP/TIFF/EPS/GIF (2D/3D) at a chosen size, resolution and antialiasing with logo/legend/axes options, for headless figure generation in batch runs and apps. Export > Data (already catalogued) exports expressions on points/grids instead.
tools.usage: Results > Export > Plot (plot1) / Image (img1); API: model.result().export().create("plot1", "Plot"); plot1.set("plotgroup", "pg1"); plot1.set("plot", "glob1"); plot1.set("filename", "C:/out/s11.txt"); plot1.run(); model.result().export().create("img1", "Image"); img1.set("sourceobject", "pg1"); img1.set("pngfilename", "C:/out/T.png"); img1.set("width", 1600); img1.run()

parameters.name: plotgroup / plot
parameters.description: Which plot's data to export (Plot).

parameters.name: filename / format
parameters.description: Output file and format (txt, csv, vtu, or image types).

parameters.name: sourceobject / width / height / resolution / antialias
parameters.description: Image source plot group and rendering settings.

parameters.name: Advanced: logo, legend, axes, title, background
parameters.description: Image content options.

tools.notes: Image export in batch mode needs comsol batch -graphics (software rendering) or a server with graphics; in MATLAB mphplot followed by print is an alternative.

tools.name: Mesh (export) / Table (export) / Player
tools.description: Remaining export nodes: Mesh writes a mesh (or a deformed/filtered dataset's mesh) to NASTRAN (.nas/.bdf), STL, PLY, 3MF, VTK/VTU, COMSOL .mphbin/.mphtxt or sectionwise text for use in other tools or re-import; Table exports a results table to TXT/CSV/DAT/XLSX (with LiveLink for Excel) including headers and units; Player generates an in-GUI animation (frames over time/parameters or rotating view) that can be exported as GIF/AVI/WebM through the Animation node (already catalogued).
tools.usage: Results > Export > Mesh (mesh1) / Table (tbl1) / Export > Animation > Player; API: model.result().export().create("mesh1", "Mesh"); mesh1.set("filename", "C:/out/m.nas"); mesh1.set("type", "nastran"); mesh1.run(); model.result().export().create("tbl1", "Table"); tbl1.set("table", "tbl1"); tbl1.set("filename", "C:/out/t.csv"); tbl1.run()

parameters.name: type (Mesh)
parameters.description: nastran | stl | ply | 3mf | vtu | comsol (mphbin/mphtxt) | sectionwise | spreadsheet.

parameters.name: Mesh source
parameters.description: A mesh sequence or a dataset (e.g. Filter dataset for topology optimisation results, deformed configuration).

parameters.name: table / filename / header / fullprec (Table)
parameters.description: Table and output formatting.

parameters.name: Player: frame selection / fps / looping
parameters.description: Animation settings.

tools.notes: STL export writes only boundary triangles; NASTRAN keeps volume elements and can be re-imported by Mesh > Import for physics on the same discretisation.

tools.name: Report / Presentation / Result Templates
tools.description: Documentation features under Results: Report generates an HTML, Microsoft Word (.docx) or (6.x) PowerPoint document of the model with Brief, Intermediate, Complete or Custom templates (title page, table of contents, model tree settings, images of plot groups, tables, equations, code), configurable per section and regenerable when the model changes; Presentation (6.2+) builds PowerPoint slides with images and tables linked to the model so they can be refreshed (also from the COMSOL add-in in PowerPoint or comsol batch -update); Result Templates (6.3) is a window/library of reusable plot groups, evaluation groups and derived values that you add to any model with one click and can extend with your own templates.
tools.usage: Results > Reports > Report (rpt1) > Write; Results > Reports > Presentation; Results toolbar > Result Templates; API: model.result().report().create("rpt1", "ReportGenerator"); rpt1.set("format", "html"|"docx"); rpt1.set("filename", "C:/out/report.html"); rpt1.run()

parameters.name: Report level / template
parameters.description: Brief | Intermediate | Complete | Custom, plus user report templates.

parameters.name: format / filename / image size
parameters.description: HTML or DOCX (or PPTX) output, image width/dpi, whether to open after writing.

parameters.name: Presentation: template, theme, image type/size
parameters.description: PowerPoint template and update settings.

parameters.name: Result Templates: add/create template
parameters.description: Insert predefined or user templates into the Results node.

tools.notes: Report sections are nodes (Title Page, Table of Contents, Section, Model Definition, Results...) that can be edited before writing; images require a graphics-capable session. In MATLAB mphreport(model, 'rpt1') writes the same report.

tools.name: d() / pd() / dtang() (differentiation operators)
tools.description: Differentiation in expressions: d(f, x) differentiates f with respect to a variable or spatial coordinate using the chain rule through all dependent variables (equivalent to the derivative suffix notation ux, uxx, uTx for first, second and mixed derivatives of dependent variables), pd(f, x) differentiates without applying the chain rule to dependent variables (partial derivative treating them as constants), and dtang(f, x) is the tangential derivative of f along a boundary or edge (projection of the gradient onto the surface), used for surface gradients, curvature-related quantities and edge fluxes. d(f, t) gives time derivatives (also ut, utt).
tools.usage: Expression syntax: d(expr, var), pd(expr, var), dtang(expr, var); suffixes: ux, uy, uz, uxx, uxy, ut, utt, uTx (derivative of T with respect to x in physics scope, e.g. Tx)

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Any expression of dependent variables, coordinates and parameters.

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: x, y, z (or r, phi), t, a dependent variable or a parameter/control variable.

tools.notes: Derivatives of Lagrange-element variables are discontinuous across elements; use ppr()/pprint() or the physics' own flux variables (ht.tfluxx) for smoother results. Derivatives with respect to parameters are zero unless the parameter is a sensitivity/control variable.

tools.name: mean() / up() / down() / side()
tools.description: Operators for quantities defined on both sides of an interior boundary: up(expr) and down(expr) evaluate the expression as defined in the adjacent upside/downside domain (relative to the boundary normal direction), mean(expr) gives the average of the two, and side(entity, expr) evaluates in a specific adjacent domain number. Needed when material properties or physics variables differ across an interior boundary (heat flux jump, material index on each side, stress on one side of a contact) or when a domain variable is plotted on an interior boundary where it is otherwise ambiguous.
tools.usage: Expression syntax: up(expr), down(expr), mean(expr), side(dom, expr); the boundary normal direction (up = direction of nx) is shown in the Selection section of boundary features

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Domain-defined expression (material property, physics variable).

parameters.name: dom (side)
parameters.description: Domain number to evaluate in.

tools.notes: For exterior boundaries up/down coincide with the single adjacent domain. Reversing the normal (Definitions > View or the feature's 'Reverse' option) swaps up and down.

tools.name: at() / with() / withsol() / withparam() / prev()
tools.description: Solution-access operators for results evaluation: with(n, expr) evaluates expr for solution number n of the current dataset (a specific time step, eigenmode or parameter index), at(t, expr) at a given time (interpolating stored steps), withsol(tag, expr) accesses the solution of any solver sequence (with setval()/setind() to pick parameters: withsol('sol2', T, setval(L, 2))), withparam(tag, expr) accesses parameter values stored with a solution, and prev(expr, i) is used inside the model (not only results) to evaluate at the i-th previous time step for explicit-in-time couplings. They make comparisons between solutions, differences from an initial state and cross-study coupling possible in plain expressions.
tools.usage: Expression syntax: with(n, expr), at(time, expr), withsol('sol2', expr, setval(param, value)), withsol('sol2', expr, setind(param, index)), withparam('sol1', expr), prev(expr, 1)

parameters.name: n / time
parameters.description: Solution number or time value.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Solver sequence tag (sol1, sol2...).

parameters.name: setval / setind / setconst
parameters.description: Choose the parameter value/index (or define a temporary constant) inside withsol/withparam.

tools.notes: withsol requires the referenced solution to exist and be on a compatible geometry; it is evaluated at postprocessing and during solving (making the dependence explicit rather than through the Jacobian). prev() only works in time-dependent solves and returns the initial value at the first step.

tools.name: nojac() / subst() / treatasconst() / test() / var()
tools.description: Operators controlling how expressions enter the equations: nojac(expr) excludes the expression's dependence on the solution from the Jacobian (the term still enters the residual) - used to break dense couplings from integration operators, to lag nonlinearities (Picard-type iteration) or to avoid Jacobian contributions from non-differentiable functions; subst(expr, var1, sub1, ...) substitutes variables inside an expression (e.g. evaluate a material function at a different temperature); treatasconst(expr) treats the expression as independent of the solution; test(expr) creates the test (weight) function for weak-form contributions and var(expr, field) restricts the test function to one field. These are the building blocks of weak contributions and custom couplings.
tools.usage: Expression syntax: nojac(expr), subst(expr, var, replacement[, var2, repl2]), treatasconst(expr), test(expr), var(expr, field)

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Expression in dependent variables.

parameters.name: var / replacement (subst)
parameters.description: Variable name and the expression replacing it.

parameters.name: field (var)
parameters.description: Dependent variable whose variation the test function corresponds to.

tools.notes: Removing Jacobian terms with nojac slows or breaks Newton convergence if the term is strongly nonlinear; a segregated solver may be needed. test() is only meaningful inside weak expressions (Weak Contribution, Weak Form PDE, Equation View).

tools.name: timeint() / timeavg() / timemax() / timemin() / integrate() / sum()
tools.description: Numerical integration and summation operators: timeint(t1, t2, expr) and timeavg(t1, t2, expr) integrate/average a time-dependent solution over an interval (cumulative energy, mean temperature over a cycle), timemax/timemin return the extreme value over the interval (with attimemax/attimemin to evaluate another expression at that instant), integrate(expr, var, lower, upper) evaluates a 1D integral of an analytic expression numerically (used in Analytic functions and variables), and sum(expr, index, lower, upper) sums an expression over an integer index (Fourier series, sums over array elements). Parametric counterparts pint/pmax/pmin/psum operate over parameter values.
tools.usage: Expression syntax: timeint(t1, t2, expr[, 'nointerp'][, tol]), timeavg(t1, t2, expr), timemax(t1, t2, expr), attimemax(t1, t2, expr1, expr2), integrate(expr, var, a, b[, tol]), sum(expr, i, 1, N), pmax(p, expr), psum(p, expr)

parameters.name: t1, t2
parameters.description: Time interval limits (must be within the stored solution).

parameters.name: expr / var / limits
parameters.description: Integrand, integration variable and bounds (integrate).

parameters.name: index, lower, upper (sum)
parameters.description: Summation index and range.

tools.notes: Time operators work in results evaluation on time-dependent datasets (they read stored steps, so store enough output times); integrate/sum work anywhere, including in the physics, but re-evaluate at every point and can be slow.

tools.name: linper() / lindev() / linsol() / lintotal() / linpoint()
tools.description: Perturbation operators used with the Frequency-Domain Perturbation, Small-Signal Analysis and prestressed studies: linper(expr) marks a load or source term as the harmonic perturbation (applied only by the perturbation solver, ignored by the stationary bias solve), while in results lindev(expr) returns the linearised deviation (the complex harmonic amplitude), linpoint(expr) the value at the linearization point (bias), lintotal(expr) the sum bias + perturbation at the current phase, linsol(expr) the standard solution, and lintotalavg/lintotalpeak/lintotalrms the cycle statistics of the total. Essential for AC analysis of MEMS, semiconductors, electrochemistry (impedance) and nonlinear magnetics.
tools.usage: In physics settings: V0 = V_bias + linper(V_ac); in results: lindev(es.V), linpoint(es.V), abs(lindev(cir.R1_i))/abs(lindev(cir.V1_v)) for small-signal impedance

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Load expression (linper) or result expression (lindev, linpoint, lintotal, linsol).

tools.notes: Without linper() the perturbation study has no source and returns zero. Bias and perturbation solutions are stored together; the dataset's 'Solution number' selects the perturbation frequency and 'phase' the instant for lintotal.

tools.name: env() / bndenv() / noenv() / dest() / reacf()
tools.description: Specialised evaluation operators: env(expr) and bndenv(expr) evaluate a field/environment expression (temperature, velocity, electric field) at the current particle or ray position in the domain or on the boundary it is interacting with, and noenv(expr) marks expressions defined only on the particles/rays themselves - the interface between Eulerian fields and Lagrangian particles/rays; dest(expr) forces evaluation on the destination side inside coupling-operator arguments (General Extrusion, Integration), e.g. intop1(exp(-(x - dest(x))^2)) for a convolution; reacf(u) returns the reaction force (Lagrange multiplier) at constrained nodes for a dependent variable, giving accurate total reaction forces and currents when integrated over a constraint boundary (solid: reacf(u), heat: reacf(T) = heat rate through a Temperature boundary).
tools.usage: Expression syntax: env(expr), bndenv(expr), noenv(expr) in particle/ray interfaces; dest(expr) inside coupling operator arguments; reacf(u) integrated over constrained boundaries (Surface Integration)

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Field expression (env/bndenv) or coupling argument (dest).

parameters.name: u (reacf)
parameters.description: Dependent variable with a Dirichlet constraint.

tools.notes: reacf requires the constraint to be applied with reaction terms (default) and is evaluated on the constrained boundaries only; with weak constraints use the Lagrange multiplier variable instead (e.g. T_lm).

tools.name: if() / nif() / isdefined() / isnan() / isinf() / try_catch() / error()
tools.description: Logical and robustness operators: if(cond, a, b) returns a where the condition is true and b elsewhere (both branches are evaluated only where needed, so if(x>0, 1/x, 0) is safe), nif(c1, e1, c2, e2, ..., eN) is the nested/else-if form, isdefined(var) is 1 where a variable exists (for expressions spanning domains with different physics), isnan/isinf test for undefined values, try_catch(expr, alt) evaluates the alternative when the first expression fails (e.g. a withsol to a missing solution), and error('msg') raises a solver error when reached (guards). Combined with the built-in smoothed step functions flc1hs(x, scale), flc2hs and flsmhs, these give differentiable switches for use inside the equations.
tools.usage: Expression syntax: if(cond, expr1, expr2), nif(c1, e1, c2, e2, else), isdefined(var), isnan(expr), isinf(expr), try_catch(expr, fallback), error('text'); smoothed Heaviside: flc1hs(x, scale), flc2hs(x, scale), flsmhs(x, scale); comparison/logical operators <, >, ==, !=, &&, ||, !

parameters.name: cond
parameters.description: Logical expression (evaluates to 0/1).

parameters.name: scale (flc*hs)
parameters.description: Half-width of the smoothing zone around 0.

tools.notes: if() with a solution-dependent condition is not differentiable at the switch, which can stall Newton iterations - prefer flc2hs (continuous first derivative) inside the physics and keep if() for postprocessing.

tools.name: realdot() / ppr() / pprint() / centroid() / adj() / sens() / fsens()
tools.description: Remaining frequently used operators: realdot(a, b) computes the time-averaged product of two complex harmonic quantities (real(a*conj(b))) with correct Jacobian for frequency-domain losses and forces (e.g. realdot(E, J)/2); ppr(expr) and pprint(expr) apply polynomial-preserving recovery to smooth derivative quantities (fluxes, stresses) on the whole mesh or within domain groups; centroid(expr) and circumcenter(expr) evaluate at element centres (element-constant plots); adj(expr) evaluates using the adjoint sensitivity solution, sens(expr, p) the forward sensitivity and fsens(p) the sensitivity of the objective with respect to control variable p after a Sensitivity/Optimization study; emetric, atlocal, gpeval, elemint/elemavg/elemgpmax handle element-level evaluations.
tools.usage: Expression syntax: realdot(a, b), ppr(expr), pprint(expr), centroid(expr), adj(expr), sens(expr, p), fsens(p), elemavg(gporder, expr), gpeval(gporder, expr)

parameters.name: a, b (realdot)
parameters.description: Complex-valued expressions in the frequency domain.

parameters.name: p (sens/fsens)
parameters.description: Control or sensitivity variable name.

parameters.name: gporder
parameters.description: Gauss point order for element-level operators.

tools.notes: Physics interfaces already provide loss and flux variables built with realdot (ec.Qh, emw.Qh); ppr should be applied to the raw derivative quantity, not to already smoothed variables.

tools.name: t / freq / lambda / phase / numberofdofs (global built-in variables)
tools.description: Reserved global variables: t is the time in time-dependent studies (in seconds; write t[1/s] to pass a dimensionless argument to a function), freq the frequency in frequency-domain/eigenfrequency results (omega = 2*pi*freq is available in most interfaces as e.g. emw.omega), lambda the eigenvalue of Eigenvalue studies (eigenfrequency studies report freq = -imag(lambda)/(2*pi) with a damping ratio from real(lambda)), phase the evaluation phase angle for complex results (set in the dataset; lintotal and instantaneous plots use it), and numberofdofs the total number of degrees of freedom of the last solved problem. Additional reserved names include timestep (current time step), niterCMP (Newton iteration counter) and gmg_level.
tools.usage: Use directly in expressions: t, freq, lambda, phase, numberofdofs, timestep; unit-aware, e.g. sin(2*pi*freq*t) in transient studies driven by a frequency parameter

parameters.name: t
parameters.description: Time (s).

parameters.name: freq
parameters.description: Frequency (Hz).

parameters.name: lambda
parameters.description: Eigenvalue (1/s), complex in damped problems.

parameters.name: phase
parameters.description: Phase angle (rad) for evaluating complex results at an instant.

parameters.name: numberofdofs / timestep
parameters.description: Solver statistics variables.

tools.notes: Do not name parameters t, freq, lambda, x, y, z, r, phi, i, j, pi, eps or inf - the built-in names take precedence and the model breaks in subtle ways. 'i' and 'j' are the imaginary unit unless redefined (COMSOL warns).

tools.name: x / y / z / r / nx / ny / nz / tx / t1x (coordinate and normal variables)
tools.description: Reserved geometric variables: x, y, z (spatial frame) and X, Y, Z (material frame, identical unless a moving mesh/deformed geometry is present), r, phi, z in 2D axisymmetry; s, s1, s2 are the edge/surface parameters (arc length or parametrisation) used as x-axis data in line graphs; nx, ny, nz (nr, nz) the outward unit normal on boundaries (direction shown in feature settings; unx/uny/unz and dnx/dny/dnz the up/down normals on interior boundaries), tx, ty, tz the edge tangent and t1x..t2z the two surface tangents; root.x etc. give the coordinates of the root (undeformed) geometry. Deformed-configuration coordinates for structural results are available through the frames and the spatial.x variables.
tools.usage: Use in expressions: x, y, z, r, phi, X, Y, Z, s, nx, ny, nz, nr, tx, ty, tz, t1x, t1y, t1z, t2x, t2y, t2z, unx, dnx...; on boundaries: normal flux = ht.tfluxx*nx + ht.tfluxy*ny + ht.tfluxz*nz

parameters.name: x, y, z / r, phi
parameters.description: Spatial coordinates (geometry length unit).

parameters.name: nx, ny, nz
parameters.description: Boundary normal components (outward from the lower-numbered domain / out of the geometry on exterior boundaries).

parameters.name: s, s1, s2
parameters.description: Curve/surface parameters.

parameters.name: tx, ty, tz, t1x..., t2x...
parameters.description: Tangent vectors.

tools.notes: Physics interfaces provide convenience normals (ht.nx, solid.nx) that agree with these; on interior boundaries the sign of nx depends on domain numbering, so use up/down or the physics' 'Reverse normal' options when the direction matters.

tools.name: h / dvol / meshvol / meshelement / meshtype / dom / qual (mesh built-in variables)
tools.description: Reserved mesh-related variables: h is the local mesh element size (length of the longest element edge; used in stabilisation, interface thickness definitions such as epsilon_pf = h/2, and in mesh-convergence plots), dvol the volume scale factor (determinant of the mapping Jacobian, with dvol_spatial for the spatial frame) that turns reference-element integrals into physical ones, meshvol the linearised element volume/area/length, meshelement the element number and meshtype the element type index (number of edges), dom the domain/boundary/edge/point number of the entity being evaluated (handy for colouring by domain or selecting by number in expressions), qual the element quality (0-1), reldetjac the relative Jacobian determinant of curved elements, and meshelementall a unified numbering. The Mesh dataset and Mesh plot make these plottable without a solution.
tools.usage: Use in expressions: h, dvol, meshvol, meshelement, meshtype, dom, qual, reldetjac; e.g. Surface plot of h to check mesh size, Filter expression dom == 3, Global Evaluation of intop1(1/dvol)

parameters.name: h
parameters.description: Local element size (m).

parameters.name: dom
parameters.description: Entity index at the evaluation level (domain number in domain plots, boundary number in boundary plots).

parameters.name: qual / meshvol / dvol
parameters.description: Quality measure, element measure, Jacobian determinant.

tools.notes: h and qual are element-wise constant; plot with 'Smoothing: none'. In moving-mesh problems dvol refers to the material frame and dvol_spatial to the deformed one.

tools.name: Variable scoping and naming (root., comp1., physics prefixes, mat1.def.)
tools.description: COMSOL variable names are scoped: dependent variables (T, u, p, V, A...) are plain names inside their component, physics-defined variables carry the interface tag (ht.tfluxx, spf.U, solid.mises, es.normE, emw.S11dB, cir.R1_i), feature-level variables add the feature tag (ht.hf1.q0, ec.term1.V0), material properties are reachable as mat1.def.k (property group def = Basic) or through the physics (ht.k_iso), operators and probes are global names (intop1, aveop1, var1), and in multi-component models variables from another component are prefixed with the component tag (comp1.T, comp2.intop1(T)); root. addresses the global scope (root.freq, root.comp1.ht.T). Physics constants (pi, eps, i, j, inf, NaN, R_const, k_B_const, c_const, mu0_const, epsilon0_const, g_const, h_const, e_const...) are always available.
tools.usage: Expression syntax: <physics>.<variable>, <physics>.<feature>.<variable>, <material>.<group>.<property>, comp1.<variable>, root.<parameter>; find names in the Equation View, the Variables tab of Results (Replace Expression), or model.result().numerical() with getExpressions in the API

parameters.name: Physics tag
parameters.description: es, ec, mf, emw, ht, solid, spf, acpr, tds, cd ... as shown in the Model Builder node label.

parameters.name: Component tag
parameters.description: comp1, comp2 ... required only across components.

parameters.name: Constants
parameters.description: *_const names for physical constants; pi, eps (machine epsilon), i/j, inf, NaN.

tools.notes: Autocomplete (Ctrl+Space) in any expression field lists valid names for the current scope. Variable names are case sensitive; units are attached automatically except in user Variables where you supply them with [unit] syntax.
